recommendations.change_to_investigate: Look for nested loops, linear searches over growing containers and recomputation of values that do not change. Replace linear membership tests with a hash set or sorted data + binary search; hoist invariant work out of loops; consider vectorization-friendly data layouts (contiguous arrays, no aliasing).
recommendations.expected_benefit: Potentially large when the complexity class changes (e.g. O(n²) → O(n log n)); modest for constant-factor tweaks.

recommendations.why_it_matters: When one function's own instructions dominate, the cost usually scales with input size inside a loop. An O(n²) pattern (e.g. a linear search inside a loop) becomes dominant quickly as n grows.
recommendations.would_disprove: If the function's self share stays the same after reducing its input size, the cost is per-call overhead rather than algorithmic growth.

facts: CPU time 8.8 s over 7.9 s wall = 1.1 cores busy on average.
2 thread(s) were observed on-CPU; the machine has 2 CPU(s), so up to 2 cores could be busy.
0 voluntary context switches (0/s), 0 involuntary.
findings.interpretation: Threads are frequently blocked rather than computing: lock contention, waiting on each other (join/condition variables) or I/O. A high voluntary context-switch rate is consistent with blocking on a contended mutex or futex.
limitations: Derived from whole-process getrusage totals; it does not say *where* threads wait.
On a busy machine, involuntary preemption also lowers utilization.
next_actions: Check whether work inside locked regions can be moved outside the lock.
Look for sync_cpu findings and pthread/futex frames in the flame graph.
Use an off-CPU tool (e.g. `perf sched`, `offcputime` from bcc) to see where threads block.

recommendations.change_to_investigate: Move computation outside the critical section, shard data per thread and merge at the end, use atomics for simple counters, or reduce how often threads must coordinate.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Can be large on multi-core machines when threads currently serialize.
recommendations.how_to_validate: Re-run the same workload with the same arguments (ideally with benchmark runs) and compare the two sessions; accept the change only if the comparison reports a significant improvement. Check that average cores busy (CPU time / wall time) increases.
recommendations.observed: CPU time 8.8 s over 7.9 s wall = 1.1 cores busy on average.
recommendations.title: Reduce lock scope and contention
recommendations.tradeoffs: Finer-grained locking increases the risk of races and deadlocks; validate with ThreadSanitizer.
recommendations.why_it_matters: Contended locks serialize threads; time blocked on a lock does not even show up as CPU samples.
recommendations.would_disprove: If CPU utilization is already close to the thread count, contention is not the limiting factor.
